title: The Hard stone in the wall
subtitle: 努力坚持 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 努力坚持（人与自我·做人与做事·努力与坚持）
meta: 主题语境：努力坚持（人与自我·做人与做事·努力与坚持）　|　核心词汇：hard　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 hard 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 the farmer wrote of ① a hard stone in the wall in the almanac, and everybody in the field said at once that it was ② harder than the one named there the year before. Three autumns on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the farmer, who never explained anything, had done it at once and gone home; it was the hard ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the hardest stone in the wall anybody in the field had ever seen, or so the almanac for September 1943 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too hard to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the child who had come to help; the hard ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the basket at the far fence, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a hard winter for the family, and said that no child in his right mind would call it ⑥ as hard as the winter for the family they had once had in the old field. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was hard or not, and he said so.

By 1956 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the almanac. What the line asked for was ⑦ something hard, and nothing besides. The child from the next field called the whole plan ⑧ quite hard; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the almanac kept the names of the hard ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1959, in the rain, she wrote of another hard stone in the wall in the same almanac, and the work, which took two autumns, seemed ⑨ harder than anybody had expected. ⑩ The hardest winter for the family in the whole field, she said in 1961, was the one she could never quite name; the hard ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 坚硬（前置定语 a hard stone in the wall：1949 年农人在农事历里记下的那件坚硬的硬石）
B. adj. 坚硬／艰难（比较级 harder than：文中两处，一处比墙里的硬石，一处比预想）
C. adj. 坚硬／艰难（最高级 the hardest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 坚硬（表语 too hard to do：母亲觉得它太坚硬，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 艰难（前置定语 a hard winter for the family：叔叔把整件事称作一桩艰难的冬天）
F. adj. 艰难（同级比较 as hard as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩家里难熬的冬天相比）
G. adj. 艰难（后置定语 something hard：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 艰难（受程度副词修饰 quite hard：那位孩子的评价）

items.q: a hard stone in the wall
the hardest stone in the wall anybody
a hard winter for the family
The hardest winter for the family in

answers.why: hard 意为“坚硬”，1949 年农人在农事历里记下的是“一件坚硬的硬石”，此处作前置定语 a hard stone in the wall。
hard 意为“坚硬”，此处用比较级 harder than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
hard 意为“坚硬”，农事历上 九月 那行字说它是田垄里最坚硬的一件，故用最高级 the hardest stone in the wall。
hard 意为“坚硬”，母亲认为这件东西“太坚硬了，谁也用不上”，too hard to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
hard 意为“艰难”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩艰难的冬天”，此处作前置定语 a hard winter for the family。
hard 意为“艰难”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩家里难熬的冬天一样艰难”，同级比较用 as hard as。
hard 意为“艰难”，农事历上那半行字要的是“艰难的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something hard。
hard 意为“艰难”，邻田垄来的那位孩子认为这套计划“相当艰难”，quite 修饰原级 hard。
hard 意为“艰难”，1959 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要艰难”，故用比较级 harder than。
hard 意为“艰难”，母亲 1961 年说的是“整个田垄里最艰难的那一桩”，故用最高级 the hardest winter for the family。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1949 年，农人在农事历里记下了一件坚硬的硬石。（a hard stone in the wall）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更坚硬。（harder than …）
母亲觉得它太坚硬，谁也用不上。（too hard to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩艰难的冬天。（a hard winter for the family）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩家里难熬的冬天一样艰难。（as hard as …）
到了 1956 年，农事历上只剩半行字：要的是一件艰难的东西。（something hard）
answers: In 1949 the farmer wrote of a hard stone in the wall in the almanac.
Everybody said it was harder than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too hard to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a hard winter for the family.
He said nobody would call it as hard as the winter for the family they had once had.
By 1956 the almanac asked for nothing but something hard.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 hard 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1949 the farmer wrote of a hard stone in the wall in the almanac, and nobody forgot it.
It was the hardest stone in the wall in the field, or so the almanac says.
My mother thought it too hard to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a hard winter for the family, and nobody argued with him.
The child from the next field called the plan quite hard, and everybody laughed.
The hard ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
